steps.name: Exhausted Guard
steps.text: There's no end to them...

steps.name: Anxious Guard
steps.text: Look out!

steps.name: Exhausted Guard
steps.text: Where did these monsters even come from, and just how many of them are there?!

steps.name: Anxious Guard
steps.text: They don't even seem to be decreasing... in fact, there's more of them now.

steps.name: Anxious Guard
steps.text: I heard last night, the third battalion in the north lost half their numbers...

steps.name: Exhausted Guard
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Anxious Guard
steps.text: Have you noticed? I don't know when it started, but these mysterious monsters are looking even more realistic than they did, and more aggressive to boot...

steps.name: Exhausted Guard
steps.text: Where's our ta ma de backup?!

steps.name: Exhausted Guard
steps.text: We're in dire straits, if this keeps up—

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: Stand up.

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: We must uphold our duty to guard the land.

steps.name: Exhausted Guard
steps.text: Imperial Guards?!

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: All units, form a line and prepare to meet the enemy.

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: There is no retreat until we annihilate all evil inside the city.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: The Grand Commandant's sickness seems to be gone... this gladdens me.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: What is it that has you looking for me at this hour?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Has Your Imperial Majesty forgotten? Just the other day, You commanded me to be here for the morning court.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I fear you must have slept to delirium... court is long over. You are late.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: No, not yet... the day of the full moon is tomorrow.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: This old servant shall accompany Your Majesty and await your order.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: ...I find myself uncertain why the Grand Commandant wants this done in haste.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: I know not what Your Majesty awaits.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: And also... what Your Majesty has planned for the day.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: That is none of your business.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Your Majesty's silence only keeps this servant guessing.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Would Your Imperial Majesty truly risk your sacred person to activate Bu Fan to settle the crisis within the Tomb of Sui?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: I know not whose slander Your Majesty has heard... to resort to such an ill-advised course.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: With no counsel offered, am I not capable of making my own decision?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Forty years ago... when Your Majesty ascended the throne, it was the Grand Tutor and I who went with you to survey Bu Fan.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: I still remember following our visit to that remote room, three whole days came and went without a single court session. To this day I remain unaware of Your Majesty's thoughts at the time.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I remember then as well... But now I no longer fear the Grand Commandant deriding me, so perhaps I shall share.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I was only thinking... in Yan's thousand year history with this object, not even once has there been a single True Lung who used it.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: If Great Yan were forced to use Bu Fan while I sat the throne... would I not become the weakest ruler in our history?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: If you would grant me a presumptuous question... If Your Imperial Majesty were to sacrifice yourself for the nation, how would it be run, subsequently?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Is there a cause for worry...? Is my replacement not already in Baizao as we speak?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: The mandarins would be unsatisfied if the deposed imperial heir Yan Wu were to take the throne, and the country would descend into chaos. And what will happen then?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: The fault will lie on the mandarins' shoulders.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: I only wish for Your Majesty to abandon this thought.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Ridiculous...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: You know well I am no match for the late emperor, whom you so admired...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Why not accept and anticipate my brother's imminent ascension to the throne, where he will be able to realize your ambitions...?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Why trouble yourself to persuade me?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Your Majesty!
The old man suddenly tenses up, his trembling voice nearly hoarse.
The man on the throne seems to have forgotten when he last saw the old man this agitated.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: For the past forty years, I have witnessed Your Majesty toil tirelessly to grow our country... not even once did you slacken from your imperial duties.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: In those years, Great Yan has enjoyed stability. Our population swelled, and the treasury remains full.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Has there been an era in our history... even more prosperous than this one... Or an emperor... more capable and benevolent than the one we have now?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: And yet, Your Majesty... do you intend to idly watch as our nation's golden age...

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Vanishes into night during this turbulent time?

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: An urgent message from the Sui Regulator. A strong energy wave has been reported from the depths of the Tomb of Sui.

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: Far stronger than the wave a hundred and twenty years ago.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: And how fare the troops and civilians?

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: Under control at the moment. Baizao's peripheral blocks moved away before the energy blast, and non-mobile settlements nearby have also been largely evacuated. The damage is minor.

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: Mt. Mang has suffered more damage, but the Tianshis are at their posts, and the Garden of Grotesqueries is still suppressing Sui.

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: There are geists running amok in the city, and the Imperial Guards are cooperating with the Patrol Battalion to establish a defense line. They will give it their all.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I see... You may go.
From behind the curtain, the True Lung rises from his throne, and descends the steps until he is next to the older man.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: It's about time.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: You may withdraw, Grand Commandant. The battlefronts of Baizao and Yumen await your commands.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty...

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: For the sake of Yan... Is Your Majesty truly unaware why I so strongly advocate for war?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Do you still remember why the court came up with the Twenty-Eight Policies?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Victoria, Leithanien, Kazdel... this whole great land is plagued by unrest, Great Yan aside.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: We are now in terrible peril... and the nation cannot afford to be passive. We must proactively seek change...

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Has Your Majesty not learned from what happened in Ursus?!

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: The Chamber of Heaven's Designs has yet to figure out what sort of power managed to wipe out that entire Originium vein.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: If the Crystal Age truly ends with the depletion of every prime vein, then Great Yan must take the responsibility and prepare to lead all of Terra.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Attack Ursus in the north, repel Victoria in the west, pacify Mitsukue and Kusarigawa in the east, and settle Rim Billiton to the south. Furthermore, we must keep a close eye on Columbia's developments as well as possible naval incursions from Ægir's own sea.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: And before all of that... while Great Yan stands at the height of its power, we must seize the chance in this fight against the bestial Sui to sweep away decades of weakness hiding under peace and prosperity!

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Only then... will we manage to stand tall in this chaotic realm... undeterred for the next millennium.
The True Lung falls silent at the old man's speech. Not only to consider all that was said, but also to calm his own mind.
No one knows how much time has passed before he finally speaks.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: You dedicated your life to wars for the country, and your military merit is without equal, but this has also left you with injuries and ailments...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Have I ever doubted your undying loyalty to the country?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: But earlier, you spoke of what befell Ursus, and that makes me wonder...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Do you remember... what happened to Gaul?

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty...?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Your words were incisive...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Yes, Great Yan should seek change, and must change...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: But the way I see it, compared to the lives we may lose to this war with the bestial Sui...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: What we need even less is a True Lung past his prime... and this power accessible only to the True Lung for the past thousand years...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: If we talk of Great Yan's future, then I must say, my outlook is indeed brighter than yours, Grand Commandant...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Has Great Yan these past forty years... lacked for loyal and righteous men?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: The Grand Preceptor, Yu Cheng, Gu Quan... the Grand Tutor, and yourself...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: My officials are loyal, my soldiers are fearless, my people are principled... Where is this 'weakness hiding under peace and prosperity' you speak of?

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: As for the future you mentioned, you can take a look in my stead...

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Your Majesty... you still insist...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: That Hunt of my ancestors' days; the remnants of the bestial Sui plaguing Yan for a thousand years... should end with me.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: If we must inevitably spill some blood...

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Then the True Lung should be the first one to spill it.
After a short silence, the True Lung walks to the doors. It has been a long time since he has stepped out of the place.
Only an old man remains in the vast palace.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: If I cannot dissuade Your Majesty, then I can only strive to serve my duty.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Send word to Yumen, it's time to make a move.
After the brief order, he disconnects the terminal and slowly walks forward.
He passes through the curtain, finally stopping before the throne, closing his eyes and staying in his spot, as if waiting for something...
Until a cough he can no longer suppress bursts from his throat.
The cough is so violent he bends over, and has to grab onto the throne for support.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You came, in the end.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: So you were here.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You don't seem surprised at all to see me, though.
Ch'en Hui-chieh is somewhat caught off-guard by her target simply showing up before her.
Still the overbearing posture, still the unfathomable look, as if they are not standing in Baizao's Forbidden City, but in the backyard of his official residence in Lungmen.
The buildings behind him seamlessly blend into his dark coat, as if those palaces are merely an excessively ornate cloak over his shoulders.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: So, at least you weren't kidnapped.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I still don't know just who on this land could manage that.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Everything I've done has been of my own volition.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I'll never stop hating that attitude of yours...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Why are you here? Is this that backup plan the Grand Tutor kept telling you to make?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: His words should not be followed entirely... the situation should never have developed as he suggested, in the first place.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I have another plan in mind.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Either way, you're safe. So what comes next won't be much of a problem.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: And what are you preparing to do?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Ensure you're safe, get you out of Baizao, then...
Ch'en casually waves the writing knife in her right hand, its simple form leaving a light yellow scroll-like afterimage in the air.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...Correct some mistakes made by you and your brother.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I see... so the artifact is with you.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I'm not too surprised.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Hah. And who were you supposing would deliver this writing knife to you?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: That's no longer important...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Since you have it, then you ought to know how to use it... and everything else about it.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I was pretty surprised. Every secret I've learned about you since coming to the city has... opened my eyes.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You know, I almost admire your ability to hide so many secrets.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: If you truly wish to rectify the mistake I made then, you should follow me.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Follow you...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Where?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Beneath the Forbidden City, to the first Originium.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: The writing knife you hold will be of use, and will solve Great Yan's crisis. All will be made right.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Of course, I prefer you hand the knife to me instead. It'll be quicker, and you'll have less trouble to contend with.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: But you won't trust me. I'm sure you want to see it all yourself before you'll give up. I don't really mind, though.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Haven't had enough of playing the tragic hero? You're just conveniently skipping over the part where you'd actually lose your life.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: We stand before a great crisis... and this is a small cost Yan can afford.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: There are no victims in this case. Your work ends here, Superintendent Ch'en.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Don't tell me you forgot. I resigned right in front of you, five years ago.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Though the man standing before me now isn't even fit to be called 'Chief Wei'.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You're telling me to watch you throw your life away, and that's not even the part of your words that's pissing me off the most.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Your sacrifice isn't going to move anyone's heart but your own.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: And right now, you don't even have the right to end your life just like that.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hui-chieh, this is no petty squabble. This matter concerns the fate of Yan and its people!

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Of course I know that...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: But get over your own ego. The country's fate doesn't fall on your shoulders alone. There are definitely other things you should be doing, besides glorifying your own suicide.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You don't have to come with me.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Give me the writing knife and go back to Lungmen.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: It's too bad I got two blades here, but I can't lend you either of them.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: We don't have any more time to lose, and you still want it your way, Superintendent Ch'en?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I'm not the one insisting on having it my way.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Must you force my hand...?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Fine, show me. Let me see how much your swordplay has grown in the last five years!

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: That's more like it.
Ch'en Hui-chieh grips the hilt of her sword.
Since she first took up the Chi Xiao, she knew this moment would one day come.
She unsheathes her blade, pointing it at the Baizao autumn breeze blowing between her and Wei Yenwu.

steps.name: Ch'en Hui-chieh
steps.text: As sword ere shadow's trace...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: ...Cast off as cast.
